name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 executable server that exposes Machai functional tools and prompts to Model Context Protocol clients. It is an orchestration and transport layer rather than a bundle of domain tools: deployments place compatible functional-tool libraries on the runtime classpath, and the server discovers, adapts, and publishes their capabilities. The single command-line entry point supports local STDIO integration as its default transport and remote HTTP integration when a port is supplied. HTTP deployments can be stateless or streamable and session-aware. The server handles command-line configuration, server identity, project-directory context, tool registration, MCP schema generation, prompt exposure, synchronous request dispatch, and Jetty-based HTTP hosting. It is suitable for connecting custom automation, coding, data, or internal-platform tools to MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, MCP Inspector, and CodeMie Code.

constructors.description: Creates the command-line application entry-point object. In normal use, invoke its static main method through the packaged executable rather than instantiating it directly.

examples.description: Step 1: build the ready-to-run distribution with Maven. Step 2: start it on port 45000; this selects HTTP MCP mode. Add compatible functional-tool jars to the runtime distribution or classpath so the server has tools to publish.

constructors.description: Creates a stateless HTTP MCP server that reports the supplied name and version to MCP clients and registers tools through the shared server infrastructure.

examples.description: Use this programmatic setup in an embedding application when a stateless HTTP transport is required. Configure the reported server identity, assign an available port, then register tools through the server lifecycle before startup.

features.name: MCP server command-line startup
features.signature: public static void org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Parses command-line options and starts the appropriate MCP transport. With no port option it uses STDIO. The --port option selects HTTP, and --session selects streamable HTTP; otherwise HTTP is stateless. Name, version, and project directory can also be supplied.

examples.description: Step 1: install or build the server jar and obtain a Machai-compatible functional-tool container jar. Step 2: put both jars on the Windows classpath. Step 3: run this command to publish the tools as a streamable HTTP MCP server at port 45000 with a project context. Step 4: configure an MCP client to use http://localhost:45000/mcp.

features.name: Configure HTTP listener port
features.description: Sets the TCP port used by an HTTP MCP server. The HTTP base implementation configures Jetty and registers its servlet transport provider when the server starts.

examples.description: For an embedded deployment, create the concrete stateless server, select an available TCP port, load the functional tools using the application lifecycle, and then start it. Clients can connect to the configured server endpoint.

features.name: Convert tool names for client display
features.description: Converts snake-case or camel-case functional-tool names into a human-readable label used when adapting Machai tool metadata for MCP clients.

examples.description: Use this helper while authoring or testing a functional-tool integration to verify the client-facing label derived from a machine-oriented tool name.

customizations.name: Functional tool and prompt libraries
customizations.description: The server intentionally contains no built-in domain tools. Add Machai-compatible functional-tool and prompt libraries to the runtime classpath; the server loads and adapts their definitions to MCP capabilities.

examples.description: Package custom functional tools with their required service-provider registration, place the tool jar beside the server jar on the classpath, and run the server in STDIO mode for a desktop MCP client.

customizations.name: Project directory context
customizations.description: The --projectDir command-line option, or AbstractMcpServer.setProjectDir, supplies a working project directory to server tools. HTTP deployments may determine it per request when no fixed directory is configured.

examples.description: Set a fixed project directory before starting a STDIO server when published tools need a known workspace for file or repository operations.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Base boundary for custom MCP server transports. Implementations provide tool registration and startup behavior while inheriting project-directory management.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer.ToolSpecificationBuilder
studs.description: Boundary for transport-specific conversion of generic MCP tools and call handlers into server tool specifications.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run an HTTP MCP server
steps: Build the runnable artifact with mvn -Ppack install, or download a release from the project SourceForge releases page.
Install or create a Machai-compatible functional-tool container and make it available beside the server artifact on the runtime classpath.
Configure the tool library prerequisites, such as provider credentials and model settings, using its documented environment variables.
Run org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer with --port 45000; add --session for streamable HTTP and --projectDir for a fixed workspace.
Configure an MCP client or mcp-remote bridge to connect to http://localhost:45000/mcp, then confirm that the supplied tools and prompts are listed.

examples.title: Run a local STDIO server for Claude Desktop
steps: Build or download the server and add its jar plus a functional-tool container jar to a stable local directory.
Configure Claude Desktop to launch java with the two-jar classpath and org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer as the main class.
Add required environment variables for the functional tools to the client configuration.
Restart the client, inspect the registered MCP tools, and invoke a tool in a project workspace.
